reader: one reader, an AI agent with read access to the benchmark databases; not reviewed by a person
method: Each of the 63 wrong answers was run beside its reference and the data queried for why they differ. For each, the engine statement was then changed in the one respect the cause names, and it returned the reference rows (counterfactualMatchesReference). The mechanisms are reproducible; the labels AMBIGUOUS, SOURCE_OPEN, MEANING and REFERENCE are judgement.

records.summary: Reads the stored rate column "Percent (%) Eligible Free (Ages 5-17)"; the reference divides the two counts.
records.settledBy: The column is type real and holds 0.904908 for the row whose counts give 295/326 = 0.9049079754. Same school, same rate, fewer digits.

records.summary: Takes "locally funded" from frpm."Charter Funding Type"; the reference takes it from schools.fundingtype.
records.settledBy: The two columns disagree on 53 of the joined rows (359 locally funded in one, 328 in the other, 320 in both). The question does not say which.

records.summary: Returns the school name beside the rate; the reference returns the rate only.
records.settledBy: The five rates are identical. Dropping the name column gives the reference result.

records.summary: Counts only rows with a school name (school IS NOT NULL): 4 to 5. The reference counts every row: 4 to 7.
records.settledBy: The 2 extra rows of the reference are district records: no school name, CDS codes 30667040000000 and 30667530000000. All 1,369 rows without a school name in the table have a code ending in seven zeros. The question asks for schools.

records.summary: Compares the 13-digit codes of the question as text; the column holds 14 digits with a zero in front. No rows.
records.settledBy: cdscode is text; the three codes exist as 01751010130583, 01612910137588, 01611760134270. Padding them gives the reference result.

records.summary: Adds mailing city, state and zip to the name and street; the reference returns name and street.
records.settledBy: Same school, same street. The question says "full mailing street address, not an abbreviated one", which the reference reads as mailstreet against mailstrabr.

records.summary: Compares the 13-digit code as text against a 14-digit column. No rows. Flagged as empty, second attempt did not replace it.
records.settledBy: The school is stored as 01611920113902. Padding gives the reference result.

records.summary: Compares the 13-digit code as text, and also requires eilname = 'High School'. No rows. Flagged as empty, second attempt did not replace it.
records.settledBy: Stored as 01611190130609, and its eilname is 'Elementary-High Combination'. Both changes are needed to reach the reference; padding alone still returns nothing.

records.summary: The inner lookup of the 13-digit code finds nothing, so the comparison is against NULL and the count is 0.
records.settledBy: With 07618040730051 the same statement returns 1, the reference value.

records.summary: Takes school type and name from the schools table (soctype, school); the reference takes them from frpm ("School Type", "School Name").
records.settledBy: The question says "the value of the field named 'School Type'", which is a literal column of frpm. For CDS 47736846050843 frpm says "Butte Valley Middle", Junior High; schools says "Butte Valley Elementary", Elementary.

records.summary: County lookup by the 13-digit code finds nothing. No rows.
records.settledBy: Padding to 01612590125716 gives the reference row.

records.summary: Returns the text '572/12'; the reference returns 47.666...
records.settledBy: Same count (572 schools). The model read "exact average without rounding" as a fraction to show.

records.summary: Compares the 13-digit code as text. No rows. Flagged as empty, second attempt did not replace it.
records.settledBy: Padding to 01612590137943 gives the reference row.

records.summary: Shows charter status as a boolean (false); the reference shows the stored 0. Every other value of the row is equal.
records.settledBy: This statement did pad the code (07618040113118). Replacing (charter = 1) by the column gives the reference row.

records.summary: County lookup by the 13-digit code finds nothing, so the second county (Alameda, 0 schools) is missing.
records.settledBy: Padding to 01100170109835 gives both rows.

records.summary: Counts 'Adult' as a lowest grade later than grade 9; the reference keeps 9 to 12 only. Two extra schools.
records.settledBy: "Low Grade" holds K, P, 1 to 12 and Adult (3 rows). The question says "grade 9 or a later grade" and does not mention Adult.

records.summary: Requires the status to be exactly 'Provision 2'; the reference accepts any status containing it. One city fewer.
records.settledBy: The one row of difference is a magnet school in Santa Barbara with status 'Breakfast Provision 2'. Whether that "runs a Provision 2 meal program" is not said.

records.summary: Ranks the frame version 'future' above every year; the reference reads it as 0 and answers 2015.
records.settledBy: frameversion holds 1993, 1997, 2003, 2015 and 'future' (93 cards, 8 of them cost 0). Nothing in the data says where 'future' sits; outside knowledge says it is the 2007 Future Sight frame.

records.summary: Tests "never on MTGO" per printing row and counts the names: 7. The reference tests it per card over all its printings: 5.
records.settledBy: Cleanse and Crusade have one printing that is paper only and another that is on MTGO.

records.summary: Adds the condition that the card is a Creature; the reference does not. 50 artists against 56.
records.settledBy: The 8 rows of difference are Artifacts with a printed power. The opening sentence says "big creatures", the list of conditions does not.

records.summary: Counts ruling rows (136); the reference counts distinct rulings by date and text (4).
records.settledBy: Fireball has 34 printings and the rulings table repeats each of the 4 rulings once per printing, with a new id each time.

records.summary: Returns the card name beside the two ids; the reference returns the two ids.
records.settledBy: The ids are identical. The question says "and nothing else".

records.summary: Groups by the column types (Creature: 71); the reference groups by the column type, the full type line (Instant: 28).
records.settledBy: By type the creatures are split by subtype ("Creature, Human Soldier" 16, "Creature, Human Knight" 8, and so on), which is why Instant comes first there.

records.summary: Reads "has a text box" as having rules text (text not empty); the reference uses the flag istextless = 0.
records.settledBy: In frame 2015, 282 printings have no text and are not textless, and 13 are textless and have text. The flag is the column that records the text box.

records.summary: Treats power as a number only when it is all digits; the reference also reads decimals.
records.settledBy: power is text and 4 rows hold '3.5' (others hold 2.5, 1.5, 0.5, *, 1+*, ?). Allowing a decimal part gives 6410.

records.summary: Counts the languages of the set's cards in foreign_data (7); the reference counts set_translations (0).
records.settledBy: set_translations has rows for 121 of 551 sets and none for Commander 2020, so the reference answers that the set was released in 0 languages. Neither figure can be confirmed from the data.

records.summary: Reads "youngest user account" as the most recently created account; the reference reads it as the lowest age.
records.settledBy: 52 accounts are named Michael and 4 have an age. Both readings are of the words as written.

records.summary: Counts distinct revisions (2 for mbq); the reference counts history rows with a comment (3).
records.settledBy: Rows 12391 and 12392 are one revision: same revisionguid, same second, same comment, one row for the body and one for the title. The question says to count every revision as its own event.

records.summary: Adds the column as consumption::NUMERIC; the reference adds it as double precision. One cent of difference in two of the three figures.
records.settledBy: consumption is type real, and in PostgreSQL a real cast to numeric keeps 6 significant digits: the stored -12606.39 becomes -12606.4.

records.summary: Computes 2012 consumption from transactions_1k (amount times price); the reference uses yearmonth.consumption.
records.settledBy: transactions_1k holds 1,000 rows from 2012-08-23 to 2012-08-26. yearmonth holds 27,676 customers in 2012.

records.summary: Returns one row per currency; the reference returns one row with two columns.
records.settledBy: The two averages are identical (3627.03 and 44462.45).

records.summary: Adds consumption::NUMERIC; the reference adds double precision. 338745675 against 338745665.
records.settledBy: Same cast as 149: 2052187.1 becomes 2052190. Changing only the cast gives the reference value.

records.summary: Looks for gasoline purchases in transactions_1k joined to products; the reference counts customers with consumption above 0 in yearmonth for 201302.
records.settledBy: transactions_1k ends on 2012-08-26, so the answer is 0 whatever the product filter. The reference does not filter by product at all, although the evidence says gasoline; no table records product by month.

records.summary: Returns the mean beside the player name; the reference returns the name.
records.settledBy: Same ten players.

records.summary: Keeps only accounts the client owns (disp.type = OWNER); the reference keeps any relation to the account.
records.settledBy: Without the condition the count is 19143, the reference value. "Accounts held by" does not say owner or any holder.

records.summary: Returns the whole ranking (11 pairs); the reference returns the top pair only.
records.settledBy: The question asks for "a ranking of the pairs" and then says "if two pairs tie for the largest total, list both".

records.summary: Uses a12 for the 1996 unemployment rate; the reference uses a13.
records.settledBy: The columns are named a2 to a16 and this run had no column descriptions. With a13 six of the eight rows match; the other two still differ by a cent because the engine averages exact decimals and the reference averages floats (east Bohemia: the average is 3.265, shown as 3.27 by one and 3.26 by the other).

records.summary: Uses a15 for crimes in 1996; the reference uses a16.
records.settledBy: Same unnamed columns. Replacing a15 by a16 gives the reference result.

records.summary: Ranks the oldest as 1; the reference ranks the youngest as 1. Every other column is equal.
records.settledBy: The question asks for an "age rank within gender" and gives no direction.

records.summary: Also requires the loan to exist by 31 December 1995; the reference dates only the account.
records.settledBy: Without the loan date the count is 13, the reference value. The question asks about the books "as of" that date.

records.summary: Averages the district salary over client and account rows; the reference averages over distinct districts.
records.settledBy: The question says "across the districts". The certificate flagged it (fanout, grain).

records.summary: Counts second-place finishes per forename; the reference counts distinct drivers.
records.settledBy: 70 second places were taken by 51 drivers. The question asks for "the number of runners-up who carried it".

records.summary: Adds four hours to the stored start time to make it local to Baku; the reference uses the stored time as local.
records.settledBy: races.time holds 13:00:00 for this race. The data does not say which zone. Outside knowledge says the race started at 17:00 local, so the stored time is UTC and the engine's figure is probably the true one.

records.summary: Returns the length in milliseconds (2011266); the reference returns the text duration (33:31.266).
records.settledBy: Same pit stop, two columns that hold the same length.

records.summary: Converts 17:00 local to 21:00 before comparing with the stored time; the reference compares with 17:00. Ten races against four.
records.settledBy: Same convention as 259. The stored times are 16:00 to 18:00, which fits UTC for a race in Montreal in the early afternoon.

records.summary: Returns the ratio beside the event name; the reference returns the name.
records.settledBy: Same three events.

records.summary: Adds up the attendance of each event of a type; the reference counts distinct members per type.
records.settledBy: Meeting: 105 attendances by 30 members. The certificate flag on this answer (period) is about something else.

records.summary: Adds a budget line once per expense; the reference adds it once per member and budget line.
records.settledBy: Four budget lines carry two expenses over 50 from the same member (three of Phillip Cullen, one of Sacha Harrison) and are added twice. The certificate flagged it (fanout).

records.summary: Keeps only events with status Closed; the reference keeps every Budget event.
records.settledBy: The missing row is Spring Budget Review, dated 2020-01-12, status Open, no attendance. The question says "has held" and the evidence names it.

records.summary: Counts members per college; the reference counts distinct majors per college.
records.settledBy: The question asks "how many majors".

records.summary: Counts attendances per event type (Meeting 109); the reference counts distinct members (Meeting 30, Registration 30).
records.settledBy: With COUNT(DISTINCT member) the same statement gives the reference result.

records.summary: Groups by the whole description; the reference splits it into items.
records.settledBy: expense_description holds lists such as 'Water, chips, cookies'. Water is on 10 records, Pizza on 7.

records.summary: Splits the items correctly and then capitalises them (Chips, Cookies); the reference keeps them as written (chips, cookies).
records.settledBy: Same items, same categories, same sums. Removing INITCAP gives the reference result.

records.summary: Returns the colour beside the name and publisher; the reference returns name and publisher.
records.settledBy: Same four heroes.

records.summary: Inner join to publisher and "name <> DC Comics" drops heroes with no publisher: 355. The reference keeps them: 358.
records.settledBy: 3 Good heroes have publisher_id NULL.

records.summary: Leaves out the condition "followed at the outpatient clinic"; the reference filters admission = '-'.
records.settledBy: admission holds +, -, '+(' and blank, and this question's evidence does not say that - is the outpatient clinic (question 417's does).

records.summary: Lists three spellings of the diagnosis; misses 'RA,SJS' (2 patients) and includes 'RA, SJS, SLE susp' (1).
records.settledBy: The reference also breaks the question's own rule: it leaves out 'RA, SJS, SLE susp' although a suspected disease "does not count", and 'SJS  RA'. By the rule as written the cohort is at least 37 patients; the reference has 35 and the engine 34.

records.summary: Returns status, patient, reading; the reference returns reading, status, patient.
records.settledBy: Same two rows in another column order.

records.summary: Accepts an examination whose diagnosis is 'SLE+Psy'; the reference splits the diagnosis on commas only and skips it.
records.settledBy: The youngest qualifying patient (2803470, born 1985) has the examination diagnosis 'SLE+Psy' and the symptom 'CNS susp'. It lists SLE.

records.summary: Requires the test date to be on or after the birthday; the reference does not, and counts a negative age as under 50.
records.settledBy: 4 patients have qualifying tests dated before their recorded birthday; 2 of them have no other qualifying test. 71 against 73.

records.summary: Returns the molecule and the bond type beside the bond id; the reference returns the id.
records.settledBy: Same six bonds.

records.summary: Returns a row for the triple bond with 0; the reference returns the two types that occur.
records.settledBy: The question lists single, double and triple. Here the engine kept the empty group and the reference dropped it, the opposite of 499.

records.summary: Inner join drops the element with no bonded atom (na); the reference returns it with 0.
records.settledBy: The question asks for each element present among the atoms.
